p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / Physical AI / FPGA accelerator reliability
p1_watchlist.why: System-level proton-irradiation study of an open-source Tensil neural-network accelerator on Zynq UltraScale+ running ResNet-20 inference, documenting availability loss and silent output corruption with implications for recovery and verifiable edge/space AI deployment. Important Physical-AI/edge accelerator reliability evidence, but not primarily an efficiency or acceleration contribution.

p1_watchlist.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / adaptive expert skipping
p1_watchlist.why: Training- and calibration-free token-adaptive expert skipping with offline spectral/prototype statistics and lightweight runtime table lookups. Strong quality at 50% expert skipping across multiple MoE LLMs, but current abstract lacks measured end-to-end systems speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: APEX-RBD: Mixed-Precision Exploration Framework for Hardware-Efficient Robot Dynamics Accelerator Design
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot accelerator / mixed precision / edge hardware
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI hardware-efficiency candidate. Automates mixed-precision design-space exploration for rigid-body-dynamics accelerators and reports up to 1.9x area reduction and 1.8x power savings across robotic platforms; valuable but focused on dynamics hardware rather than learned policy serving.

p1_watchlist.title: Deep Microcompression: Structured Pruning and Bit-packed Quantization for Microcontrollers
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / microcontroller inference / pruning / quantization
p1_watchlist.why: Hardware-aware MCU deployment pipeline combining structured pruning, QAT and fixed-length bit-packing; reports 55.8x weight compression and deployment on ATmega328P with 2KB SRAM. Valuable edge-AI systems signal but currently limited-model/MCU scope.

p1_watchlist.title: GreenPipe: Power Modeling for Containerized DNN Inference on Kubernetes Edge Nodes
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud heterogeneous AI systems / Kubernetes inference / online power modeling / energy-aware serving
p1_watchlist.why: 30d edge/heterogeneous replay recovered a current containerized inference systems paper absent from authority/watch. GreenPipe builds an automated external-meter profiling, regression-model training and validation pipeline for Raspberry-Pi/K3s DNN serving, covering precision/thread/local-vs-remote configurations and jointly reporting latency and energy. Retained as high-value watch because it is primarily measurement/modeling infrastructure rather than a new serving scheduler or accelerator mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multimodal reasoning / CoT compression / KV pressure
p1_watchlist.why: Strong efficiency signal for multimodal reasoning: fewer than 900 training samples, up to 69.5% CoT-length reduction and up to 3.34x end-to-end inference speedup while preserving accuracy. Contribution is primarily algorithmic preference/compression rather than a serving-system design, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Compact-Memory LLM Agents via Online Max-Member Clustering and Atom-Aware Packing
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory compression / long-horizon agents
p1_watchlist.why: Online clustered memory reaches 83% of full-context quality at 32% of token cost under a 4k budget and improves over streaming-cluster baselines; relevant to efficient long-horizon agents, though current evidence is token-budget efficiency rather than serving-system latency.

p1_watchlist.title: Fast Gauss Sums via Flash Attention
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / efficient attention reuse
p1_watchlist.why: Maps arbitrary signed Gaussian kernel sums onto FlashAttention using small input augmentations, outperforming compiled PyTorch and PyKeOps for D>8 in fp16 while keeping linear memory scaling; useful kernel-reuse result, but it targets kernel methods rather than mainstream AI-inference workloads.

p1_watchlist.title: Cache-Aware Joint Router Adaptation for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / expert cache / router adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Direct MoE inference memory/traffic optimization using jointly adapted temporal and spatio-temporal cache routers while preserving native Top-K; reports 4.6-53.3% expert-weight traffic reduction. Watch pending venue/adoption evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: Reasoning Without Inference Cost: Latent Semantic Scaffolding for Robot VLA Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / zero-overhead reasoning / deployment efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI signal. Training-only semantic scaffolding aligns action-token representations to physical-reasoning rationale embeddings and drops the projection head at deployment, leaving the base VLA with zero added inference cost. Strong deployment-efficiency idea but primarily algorithmic and currently preprint-only, so high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Coupled Control and Wireless World Models for Resilient Remote Robotic Control
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / cloud-edge robotics / communication-aware world models
p1_watchlist.why: Couples control and wireless JEPA world models to predict robot and channel state and schedule uplink transmissions, explicitly targeting communication-efficient remote robotic control; currently validated in Gazebo-ROS-Sionna simulation rather than production deployment.

p1_watchlist.title: Linguistic Trajectory Encoding for Efficient Long-Horizon Spatial Memory in Embodied Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / embodied agent memory / long-horizon spatial compression
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI memory-efficiency watch. LTE compresses per-object motion histories using language plus sparse spatial/visual anchors, adapting representation to motion complexity. The paper reports 8.7x-26.1x trajectory compression with sub-second queries over 24-hour video and substantial retrieval gains. Valuable for embodied long-context/memory census, though it is a memory representation rather than a full VLA/WAM serving runtime.

p1_watchlist.title: ProtLingo: Efficient Protein Language Modeling via Conditional Memory and Expert Routing
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / conditional memory / efficient language models
p1_watchlist.why: Combines conditional local memory with sparse expert routing in a protein language model and activates only a subset of expert parameters. Interesting efficiency mechanism, but primary evidence focuses on parameter/task efficiency rather than end-to-end systems latency or throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Diffusion Language Models for Mobile Edge Agentic AI: Foundations, Applications, and Challenges
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / diffusion language models / edge-cloud serving / mobile edge AI
p1_watchlist.why: 30d edge/agent replay recovered a systems-oriented survey absent from the authority union. It connects DLM parallel refinement and quality-latency elasticity to edge constraints including memory, energy, bandwidth, split inference, communication-aware serving, long-context state, and multimodal grounding. High lineage value, but its primary contribution is survey/taxonomy rather than a new runtime mechanism, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / prefix cache / quantization / reproducibility
p1_watchlist.why: Direct serving-path measurement showing prefix-cache state can materially change multi-turn agent trajectories, with divergence increasing from 36.2% at 16-bit to 75.0% at 4-bit across two engines. Important cache+quantization systems reliability signal, but it is primarily a measurement/reproducibility study and currently only submitted to IEEE Access, so keep as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Sustainable Edge Vision via Empirically Calibrated DVFS: Eliminating Thermal Throttling on Passively Cooled Hardware
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / DVFS / thermal-aware inference
p1_watchlist.why: Real hardware edge-inference scheduler on passively cooled Raspberry Pi 5. Eliminates observed thermal throttling, improves frame rate by 6.8% versus temperature-only control and reduces energy/frame by 1.9%; scope is narrow, so high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: Importance-Aware Low-Rank Distillation of Diffusion Transformers
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / model compression
p1_watchlist.why: SVDtrunc allocates low-rank compression across DiT blocks and retains near-full FLUX.dev quality at 68% of original parameter count while remaining competitive at 57%; strong deployment-efficiency signal but no direct measured latency/throughput result in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: JLIR: A Julia-Native MLIR-Inspired Intermediate Representation with Automatic JACC Kernel Extraction
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / Julia IR / accelerator kernel extraction
p1_watchlist.why: Compiler-infrastructure contribution bringing MLIR-style extensible IR into Julia with automatic JACC accelerator-kernel extraction. Relevant to DSL/compiler route, but current primary evidence does not yet establish strong AI-workload performance impact.

p1_watchlist.title: Training-Free Halving of Activated Experts in Fine-Grained Mixture-of-Experts Models
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / expert pruning / inference efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free method separates active expert count from probability-mass normalization, halving routed-expert compute on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with only 0.35 MMLU-point loss and replicating on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Strong algorithmic MoE-efficiency signal but lacks measured serving latency/throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs) for Post-Deployment Physical AI
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / on-device adaptation / post-deployment runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI deployment signal. CFAM performs autonomous gradient-free on-device post-deployment updates across five embodiments and reports 2.5x fewer prior-training trajectories plus +13.9pp action success after near-OOD field updates. Systems/deployment relevance is real, but the contribution remains model/learning-framework heavy and lacks a strong systems venue, so high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: When Quantization Breaks Memory: Recurrent-State Write-Back in Low-Precision Temporal Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / recurrent-state memory / inference reliability
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that deterministic 4-bit recurrent-state storage can catastrophically amplify error over time, and that error-feedback/residual-memory write-back can recover accuracy without retraining. The result is domain-specific but exposes a general systems interface issue for low-precision stateful inference.

p1_watchlist.title: FAVE: Foveated Adaptive Visual Encoding for Efficient Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / visual-token efficiency / adaptive encoding
p1_watchlist.why: Strong MLLM efficiency signal: variable-resolution foveated encoding, 12.7x lower FLOPs in a controlled small-object setting and 3.3x controlled TTFT speedup when integrated with FastVLM. Current contribution is primarily model/encoding design rather than a full serving-system paper, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / local inference / distillation
p1_watchlist.why: Fresh efficiency-adjacent work that compiles recurring natural-language functions into reusable compact local neural functions, avoiding repeated remote LLM calls and their latency/cost/provider dependency. Strong deployment motivation but no broad end-to-end systems benchmark yet, so retain as P1 watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: TAP-Path: Task-Adaptive Structural and Token Pruning for Efficient and Trustworthy Pathology Foundation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / multimodal models / efficient inference
p1_watchlist.why: Combines transformer-block removal and adaptive patch-token pruning, reducing encoder parameters by about 25% and analytical compute by 35.2% while preserving or improving pathology accuracy. Strong compression signal but currently domain-specific and without measured systems latency.

p1_watchlist.title: Flip, Don't Shuffle: Watermarking LLMs at the Speed of Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / inference kernel / watermarking overhead
p1_watchlist.why: Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking reduces token membership to O(1), supports single-kernel execution with zero intermediate allocations and distributed inference, and reports <1% end-to-end generation overhead. Accepted at EMNLP 2026 Main, but watermarking is adjacent rather than a core serving primitive, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Lngram v2: Latent N-Gram Memory with Interpretable Discrete Representations
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / multimodal serving / conditional memory / efficient model architecture
p1_watchlist.why: Promising efficient memory mechanism that decouples route count, memory dimension and backbone width, with grouped-query readout and hard discrete addressing. Scales to a 30B VLM while substantially reducing total and activated memory parameters, but current evidence emphasizes model/parameter efficiency rather than measured serving latency or throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: SGD-KV: Summarization Guided KV Cache Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context
p1_watchlist.why: Head-aware KV-cache compression using summarization-head diagnostics; evaluated on Qwen2.5-7B-1M and Qwen3-32B up to 1M context with up to 75% KV-memory reduction. Retained P1 because current evidence is primarily algorithmic memory/accuracy rather than an end-to-end serving runtime.

p1_watchlist.title: Who Speaks for the Pruned? Visual Token Pruning as Coverage Optimization
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / sparsity/pruning / visual token pruning
p1_watchlist.why: CoverPruner formulates training-free visual-token pruning as representational coverage maximization and reports the best average accuracy across multiple VLMs and compression rates, especially under aggressive pruning. It directly targets inference cost, but the current abstract does not provide end-to-end latency or throughput measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: RACE-AIMC: Selective Inference for Heterogeneous Analog In-Memory Accelerators at the Edge
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / analog in-memory accelerator / selective inference
p1_watchlist.why: Relevant heterogeneous edge-AI accelerator routing framework with certified selective inference and modeled 69.02% energy reduction versus always running all accelerators, but current evidence is simulation-only and lacks a strong systems venue, so retain as high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: Compute-in-Memory Attention: A Time-Domain Analog Softmax Circuit with RC-Tunable Temperature
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / AI accelerator / compute-in-memory / analog softmax
p1_watchlist.why: Relevant attention-accelerator circuit that eliminates an intermediate ADC path by applying tunable time-domain analog softmax directly to CIM score voltages. Post-layout 22-nm simulations report 242.97 ns, 13.44 mW and 25.5 pJ/output element for 128-way softmax, with hardware-aware Transformer loss within 2.5% of ideal. Simulation-only evidence keeps it watchlist-high rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: GPU-Accelerated Astrodynamics World Models for Spacecraft Rendezvous and Proximity Operations
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / GPU simulation
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces an open-source JAX GPU-parallel spacecraft environment and a flow-matching world model for autonomous rendezvous, with improved sample efficiency and docking success. It is a useful Physical-AI world-model/runtime signal, but not yet a serving or deployment-efficiency paper.

p1_watchlist.title: Quality Recovery for Quantized KV Caches via Low-Rank Attention Adaptation
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache / quantization / long-context inference / low-rank adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: High-value KV-quantization watch item. It keeps physically packed low-bit cache formats fixed and distills floating-cache behavior into low-rank Q/K/V projection updates, recovering substantial held-out perplexity gaps across multiple models/quantizers while showing that perplexity recovery does not necessarily recover long-context retrieval. Useful evidence for quantized-KV deployment tradeoffs, but currently narrower and more adaptation-centric than a new serving runtime mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / LLM compression
p1_watchlist.why: Extends SparseGPT with a bias-aware second-order term and evaluates 25%, 50%, and 2:4 structured sparsity while preserving perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Relevant pruning follow-up, but the primary contribution is fairness-quality rather than measured runtime/system acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: Scalable Kronecker-Fisher Approximation: Efficient Hessian Analysis for Billion-Parameter Language Models Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / sparsity / compression / Hessian-Fisher analysis
p1_watchlist.why: Scalable Kronecker-based Fisher/Hessian approximation captures cross-layer sensitivity for billion-parameter models without materializing the full matrix and correlates with degradation/recovery under quantization and sparsification. Useful for mixed-precision and sparsity allocation, but current contribution is analysis/methodology rather than demonstrated end-to-end serving acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: LookStep: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation with Linguistic Foresight and Event Driven Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embodied navigation / bounded memory
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI efficiency signal. Replaces accumulated frames/cognitive maps with event-driven bounded rolling memory and linguistic future-state modeling; reports 49.7% R2R-CE Val-Unseen success with better memory efficiency and less data, with official author code/model release. Current paper emphasizes policy/task quality more than measured end-to-end serving latency, so keep as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Efficient GUI Agents: A Systems Survey of Observation, Memory, Action, and Runtime Optimization
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / GUI agents / runtime optimization
p1_watchlist.why: High-value efficient-agent systems survey. It frames deployment efficiency end-to-end across observation, context/memory, action budget and planner/runtime overhead, with explicit attention to selective reading, recoverable memory, verification-aware control and hybrid GUI/non-GUI runtimes. Keep for lineage and recall expansion; survey contribution does not justify canonical mechanism promotion.

p1_watchlist.title: SCX Router: Streaming Zero-Shot Model Selection with a Decoder-KV Classifier and a Real-World Task Ontology
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / model routing / KV-cache reuse
p1_watchlist.why: Lightweight 0.6B zero-shot inference router preserves decoder KV across sessions and evaluates transient candidate labels without polluting persistent cache; directly relevant to serving model selection, but current primary evidence emphasizes routing quality rather than end-to-end latency/cost measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: GeoSPRINT: Geometric Redundancy-Aware Step Pruning for Inference in Diffusion Trajectories
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / inference-step pruning
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free diffusion acceleration via geometric redundancy-aware nonuniform sampling schedules. Improves FID over uniform DDIM at matched NFE budgets across CIFAR-10, LSUN Church and Stable Diffusion v1.5; promising algorithmic acceleration but no direct wall-clock/runtime systems evidence yet.

p1_watchlist.title: XMerge: Cross-Axis Selection and Reconstructive Layer Merging for LLM Depth Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / LLM compression / serving
p1_watchlist.why: XMerge removes complete transformer layers while preserving the standard serving architecture and reconstructs local boundaries to reduce quality loss. It reports decode savings sufficient to amortize construction cost after tens of thousands of requests, but lacks a strong end-to-end production serving benchmark.

p1_watchlist.title: Modeling What Changes: Sparse, Residual World Models for Object-Centric Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / sparse world models / object-centric prediction
p1_watchlist.why: Sparse change-gated residual world model predicts only changing objects, giving 8.6-11.1x fewer parameters and 2.5-4.6x better next-state pose accuracy than a dense baseline on 3-8 object MuJoCo pushing, with lower rollout drift and cross-object-count transfer. Strong Physical-AI efficiency signal, but planning success remains early and no deployment/runtime latency is shown, so retain as protected high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: HeadWiseKV: Budgeted Per-Head Cache Residency for Hybrid Long-Context Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / LLM serving
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free per-head KV residency allocation for hybrid long-context language models. Grouped-cache runtime physically materializes reduced per-head residency; Qwen3.6-27B systems study reports 8.59% lower sampled peak device memory at 112K context and extends verified maximum context from 114K to 161K. Directly relevant to KV-cache/long-context serving, but current systems gains are moderate, so retained as high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: Post-Training Ternarization of Qwen3-4B Capability, Effective Bit Budget, Storage Compression, and Deployment
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / LLM deployment / edge systems
p1_watchlist.why: This study converts Qwen3-4B to 1.641 effective bits per quantized linear weight and packs the model from 8.29 GiB to 3.96 GiB, explicitly auditing deployment behavior. It is valuable as a negative systems result because its preliminary Triton GEMV is 4.6x slower than FP16 cuBLAS, showing storage compression does not automatically yield inference speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Network-Aware Forecasting on Wireless Access Points
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / on-device inference / resource contention
p1_watchlist.why: Useful real deployment measurement for inference sharing an enterprise AP with packet processing. Five implementations run 6.1-19.1x slower on target AP than Raspberry Pi 5; two similarly sized foundation models differ 19x in AP latency; 13-stream serving under network saturation raises p99 RTT 76% and cuts throughput 7.06%. Primarily a measurement/deployability study rather than a new runtime, so watchlist-high.

tracking_records.why: Long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory traffic because dense self-attention computes quadratic query-key scores. By routing all legal tile groups, TileMix preserves dense token connectivity, requires no training, and supports grouped-query attention, variable-length batches, and INT8 key/value caches. Across LongEval, LV-Eval, and A100 prefill benchmarks on LLaMA, Qwen, and Vicuna, TileMix recovers long-context quality lost under uniform INT8 and improves prefill throughput over FP16, yielding a controllable accuracy-efficiency frontier across model families. tracking_records.title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes
tracking_records.topic: MoE expert-parallel load balancing / serving
tracking_records.why: In expert-parallel (EP) MoE serving, every layer synchronizes at the slowest GPU. Dispatchers balance token counts (EPLB, LPLB, UltraEP) or activated-expert counts (METRO), assuming expert time is linear in one. Measurements on two datacenter GPU generations show it is neither: below $n^* \approx 156$--$168$ tokens, HBM weight streaming dominates---cost attaches to $activated replicas$, not tokens; above it, grouped GEMM rounds tokens to 128-tile $M$-tiles, so $splitting$ an expert adds padded compute. A max-affine profile $t=\max(a+bG,\,c+βN)$ captures both regimes. Realistic decode batches hold hot experts in the linear regime and cold in the flat $simultaneously$; recorded batches show proxy dispatches differ by $1.4$--$1.6\times$ in modeled block time (p95 up to $1.7\times$), and $which$ proxy wins flips with the regime. We formalize per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem---NP-hard on two fully replicated GPUs, polynomial in degenerate limits---and present TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher solving it in milliseconds off the critical path; its SGLang integration runs out-of-process and fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel. Anchored by an 8-GPU Testbed A microbenchmark, TEMPO stays within $1\%$ of the best fixed baseline everywhere and wins by up to $15.5\%$ where regimes mix. End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B (inside the win region) gains $4$--$6\%$ throughput and cuts p99 latency by $\sim 15.6\%$; DeepSeek-V3 (outside, communication-dominated) shows only mechanism cost. A phase diagram, not a universal win, is the claim: it predicts both outcomes before deployment.

tracking_records.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
tracking_records.topic: sparse video attention / DiT inference
tracking_records.why: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) incur quadratic self-attention cost over spatiotemporal tokens. Existing training-free sparse attention methods often construct sparse masks from block-level or cluster-level proxy scores, which can obscure fine-grained differences among keys and miss high contribution keys under aggressive sparsity. Moreover, such proxy scores may yield overly concentrated softmax distributions, causing Top-$p$ to retain too few keys for some query clusters. Although a fixed Top-$k$ minimum alleviates this failure mode, a shared value cannot adapt to variations across heads and inputs. To address both limitations, we propose SCOPE, a training-free sparse attention framework that combines 3D-RoPE-aligned key subspace clustering with online per-head Top-$k$ estimation for efficient video-DiT inference. SCOPE partitions post-RoPE keys into temporal, height, and width subspaces, clusters them independently, and aggregates the corresponding centroid scores through lookup tables to obtain per key proxy scores for each query cluster. Building on existing hybrid Top-$p$/fixed Top-$k$ selection, SCOPE derives a head-specific Top-$k$ value online by averaging the initial retained key counts within each head, weighted by query cluster size, and selects additional keys only for query clusters whose initial retained key counts fall below this value. Sparse attention is then computed over the selected original keys and values. Across six model--task configurations, SCOPE consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines in both fidelity and latency, achieving up to a $1.99\times$ end-to-end speedup on 720p HunyuanVideo with $28.46$ dB PSNR relative to dense attention.

tracking_records.title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix
tracking_records.topic: KV-cache paging / multi-agent serving
tracking_records.why: Production paged-serving engines apply uniform paging granularity to the KV cache, even though the two regions of a multi-agent workload have opposite storage requirements: a long shared prefix demands contiguity, while the per-request suffix demands fine-grained allocation. At $L_p{=}16$\,K shared tokens GraniKV reaches $\mathbf{2.16\times}$, $\mathbf{1.98\times}$, and $\mathbf{1.57\times}$ output-token throughput over the production baseline on Llama-3.1-8B/TP=1, Qwen-2.5-14B/TP=2, and Qwen-2.5-32B/TP=4. tracking_records.title: Global Simulation-Guided Dynamic Operator Scheduling for Efficient Multi-Tenant Model Serving
tracking_records.topic: multi-tenant model serving / operator-level scheduling
tracking_records.why: Container-granularity scheduling leaves abundant short-lived idle slices within containers unexploited. Reallocating containers is too heavyweight to utilize such fine-grained opportunities under SLA constraints, and operator-level scheduling requires reasoning about dependencies, memory safety, and cluster-wide execution dynamics in real time. In this paper, we present SliceScheduler, a dynamic operator-level scheduling system for multi-tenant model serving. The key idea is to expose cluster-wide operator execution state and enable what-if reasoning over scheduling decisions. SliceScheduler consists of four key components. First, we introduce the Global Mapping Graph (GMG), a unified abstraction that captures operator dependencies, tensor shapes, resource mappings, and execution states, providing a real-time, cluster-wide view with explicit resource semantics. Second, we build a global simulator on top of GMG to predict operator-level execution and memory evolution under candidate placements. Third, we design an incremental, simulation-based scheduling module that selects placements to exploit fragmented idle slices while avoiding memory violations and preserving SLA. Finally, we develop an operator executor that materializes scheduling decisions on GPUs and coordinates computation and cross-accelerator transfers. We implement SliceScheduler as a PyTorch backend and evaluate it using production trace replay. Experimental results show that SliceScheduler improves token throughput by 1.10--2.29$\times$ compared to existing approaches, while maintaining SLA violations within 9\%. SliceScheduler demonstrates that operator-level scheduling is a practical and effective approach to improving GPU utilization for multi-tenant LLM serving.

tracking_records.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
tracking_records.topic: diffusion cache policy / video-image generation acceleration
tracking_records.why: Diffusion models have achieved dominant performance in visual generation but suffer from substantial inference overhead. While cache-based acceleration has emerged as a promising solution, existing policies rely on local similarity heuristics, which we identify as being significantly misaligned with final generation quality. This discrepancy stems from the non-uniform propagation and accumulation of errors along the denoising trajectory. To address this, we propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache). We first establish a rigorous theoretical characterization of the error propagation upper bound. Recognizing that this bound can be overly conservative for complex, highly non-convex diffusion models, we further reparameterize the propagation exponent with a Bernstein form and reformulate cache policy search as a bilevel optimization problem. In detail, GCache identifies an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning the error-weighting function with generation quality loss in the outer objective. This framework effectively reconciles theoretical rigor with empirical performance, learning to prioritize computation where it most impacts visual fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCache consistently outperforms prior caching strategies on both video and image generation. Notably, on the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache maintains a 2.17x speedup while significantly enhancing generation quality, reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.

tracking_records.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
tracking_records.topic: agentic serving characterization / systems benchmark
tracking_records.why: Agentic applications are shifting AI serving from isolated model inference to long-running workloads in which LLMs coordinate tools, environments, and persistent state. However, the system behavior of these workloads---where latency, cost, and bottlenecks arise---remains poorly characterized, leaving serving systems to rely on assumptions built for conventional inference. We present AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit with ten representative agentic applications and unified systems-level instrumentation. Across controlled deployments and production traces, we identify six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM serving: (1) execution is heavyweight and stateful, with non-LLM components dominating latency in 5 of 10 applications and sandbox working-set memory peaking at 28 GB per session; (2) applications compose components with heterogeneous resource affinity---GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, CPU-bound sandboxes---whose task latencies diverge by up to 32x; (3) bottlenecks shift across requests, models, and deployments; (4) production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps; (5) a control-plane tax---auxiliary LLM calls and context overhead from tool schemas and observations---crowds out productive compute and context; and (6) production traces from three applications reveal heavy cross-request redundancy in search queries and web fetches, exposing a large caching opportunity. Four design explorations demonstrate that these findings are actionable: task-aware serving reduces latency by 29--40%, communication-aware placement by up to 4.5x, state offloading reduces memory usage by 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls and saves 19.3% of aggregate search latency.

Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

tracking_records.title: Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Efficient VLA Inference via Speculative Inference and Verification
tracking_records.topic: VLA speculative inference / algorithm-architecture co-design
tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in the field of embodied AI, but their high computational cost and limited predicted action length hinder real-time deployment. Although Dadu-Corki, a dedicated accelerator for efficient embodied AI, has been introduced, it does not exploit the inherent interaction patterns between the robot and its environment, which results in a relatively short predicted action length. We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the algorithm side, SpecVLA introduces a state-aware VLA inference execution paradigm and a hardware-friendly construction of a smaller verification model (sVLA) using differential residuals and block-wise mixed-precision quantization. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. By enabling long-action-length speculative prediction with timely verification, SpecVLA achieves real-time robotic manipulation with both high efficiency and reliability.
